key_insight: EgoGeneralist adapts pretrained video generators to connect first-person video with human motion in metric 3D space. One model supports action-controlled video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation.
problem_solved: Modern video models have strong visual understanding but lack a native representation of physically scaled 3D human motion, making it difficult to connect actions and egocentric video in both directions.
method: Adapt pretrained video generators for unified egocentric action-video modeling.
Use a role-adaptive action renderer to express metric 3D motion in a video-native representation.
Treat motion as either a spatial control input or a recoverable output, enabling action-to-video, video-to-pose, and joint generation.
impact: The approach offers practitioners a unified foundation for motion-controlled first-person video synthesis and pose recovery, rather than separate task-specific models. It connects video-generation priors with explicit 3D action representations.
visual_elements: Three-branch diagram showing action-to-video, video-to-pose, and joint action-video generation.
Pipeline illustrating 3D motion → role-adaptive action renderer → pretrained video generator.
Paired first-person video frames and 3D skeletons to illustrate the action-video connection.
Bidirectional arrows highlighting motion as both a control input and a predicted output.
paper_title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
paper_authors: Yanlin Jin, Bowen Yang, Cheng Zhang, Yifan Yang, Zhe Li
